(I)--(देवकभोजपुत्री Suna1ma1) a Bhoja princess; a daughter of Devaka, one of the wives of Vasu- deva and mother of eight sons of whom कृष्ण was one, all of them comparable to the eight Vasus;
1: भा. I. 1. १२; III. 1. ३३; 2. २५; IX. २४. २३, ४५, ५३; X. 1. 8 and २९; ३६. १७; Br. I. 1. १२५; M. ४४. ७३; ४६. १३-15; ४७. 2; वा. 1. १४८; ९६. १६३, १७२-4; Vi. IV. १४. १८; १५. १८. २६-30.
oppressed by Kamsa and relieved by कृष्ण; was about to be murdered by Kamsa who heard a divine voice that her eighth child would be the cause of his end; on Vasudeva's assurance to give up the babies as they were born she was allowed to go. Her first child कीर्तिमत् was taken to Kamsa who returned the baby. She was imprisoned with Vasudeva to watch over the birth of her sons. During her seventh pregnancy the धाम of Hari in her womb was transferred by योगमाया to that of रोहिणी and it was said that देवकी aborted. Then the अम्श of Hari entered her womb and she grew beautiful every day. ब्रह्मा, शिव and other Gods waited on her on the eve of कृष्ण's birth and said that her son was to kill [page२-114+ ३८] Kamsa: addressed the new-born कृष्ण. In the स्वायम्- bhuva epoch she was पृश्नि and Vasudeva was Sutapa. In another epoch she was Aditi and Vasudeva was कश्यप. यशोदा's daughter exchanged for देवकी's son and Kamsa was told of the birth of a girl; was released from prison along with Vasudeva; forgave and advised Kamsa; was saluted by कृष्ण and राम.

(I)--the daughter of शुक्र and ऊर्जस्वती (यजनी, जयन्ती); accompanied शर्मिष्ठा, the Asura king's daughter to water-sports; when शर्मिष्ठा clothed herself [page२-122+ ३७] with देवयानी's dress by mistake, देवयानी treated her as a slave, she being the daughter of a Brahmana Purohita. The Princess became enraged, stripped her and cast her into a well and went away; when she was crying helpless there came ययाति who was on a hunting expedition. He gave her his upper cloth to wear and lifted her up. देवयानी request- ed him to be her husband, saying that she had been cursed by Kaca, बृहस्पति's son, to marry only a क्षत्रिय. ययाति agreed and departed. देवयानि reported शर्मिष्ठा's con- duct to her father शुक्र who left the palace in disgust. The king implored him on his knees, when शुक्र agreed to stay on if शर्मिष्ठा would be appointed as servant of his daughter. This was agreed upon, and शर्मिष्ठा became her servant. When देवयानी was married to ययाति, शुक्र presented शर्मिष्ठा as his daughter's maid. She had two sons Yadu and Turvasu. Learning of her husband's connec- tion with शर्मिष्ठा during her own pregnancy, देवयानी left for her father's house. ययाति followed her and was cursed by शुक्र to fall a prey to old age. ययाति appealed to him to mitigate the curse as his desire for enjoyment with his daughter was still keen. Then शुक्र said that if anyone would give him his youth and take up old age then he could regain his youth. His son पूरु agreed and once more the king enjoyed the company of देवयानी;

--a territorial division of शाल्मलिद्वीप. भा. V. २०. 9.
(I)--a son of Rudra (putra) सावर्णि (ऋथुसा- वर्ण-वा। प्।) Manu. भा. VIII. १३. २७; Br. IV. 1. ९४; वा. १००. ९८; Vi. III. 2. ३६.
(II)--a son of अक्रूर and उग्रसेनी. भा. IX. २४. १८; Br. III. ७१. ११३; M. ४५. ३१; Vi. IV. १४. १०.
(III)--a son of Devaka. भा. IX. २४. २२; Br. III. ७१. १३०; M. ४४. ७२; Vi. IV. १४. १७.
--a daughter of Meru and queen of केतुमाला. भा. V. 2. २३.

--a name of भीष्म (s.v.); knew the yoga power of विष्णु;
1: भा. I. 9. 1; II. 7. ४४.
son of शन्तनु and जाह्नवी.
2: M. ५०. ४५.

--the chief among the Brahmanas who in appreciation of the wood-cutter's charities renamed him [page२-127+ २५] Dvijavarma and his wife शीलवती; for this the wood-cutter had a town founded in the Brahmana's name, the Purohita who honoured him with a high status. Br. IV. 7. ३१, ३७.
(I)--a son of शोणाश्व. M. ४४. ७९.
(II)--a disciple of Rathitara (s.v.). वा. ६०. ६६.
(I)--a son of देवमीढ and मारीषा; husband of कम्सवती and father of two sons. भा. IX. २४. २८, ४१. Vi. IV. १४. ३०.
(II)--a कौशिक and a Sage. Br. II. ३२. ११८.
(III)--a son of शूर and भोजा. Br. III. ७१. १४९; M. ४६. 2.
(IV)--the son of देवरात according to the learned. वा. ९६. १८५; Br. III. ७१. १८८.
--the brother of Vasudeva. वा. ९६. १४७. [page२-134+ २५]
--a son of Manu रुद्रसावर्णि (ऋथुसा- वर्ण, वा। प्।). भा. VIII. १३. २७; Br. IV. 1. ९४; वा. १००. ९८; Vi. III. 2. ३६.

--is वैकृत: different species: Gods, पितृस्, Asuras, Gandharvas, Apsarasas, Siddhas, यक्षस्, राक्षसस्, [page२-128+ ३१] चरणस्, भूतस्, Preta-पिशाचस्, विध्याधरस्, Kinnaras, etc.
1: भा. III. १०. १६, २६-8.
The sixth sarga.
2: वा. 6. ६३.
--the thirteenth Manu; father of Citra- sena, and others; Divaspati is Indra. Nirmoka and others were sages; योगेश्वर is Hari's manifestation. भा. VIII. १३. ३०-32.
--a class of पितृस् among whom four divi- sions are distinguished; the past, the future, the elder and the younger. वा. ७१. १५-16.
--a daughter of Indra, married to कुमार. Br. IV. ३०. १०५; M. १५९. 8.

(I)--heaven, etc. for वर्णाश्रमिस्; eight places beginning with ब्रह्मा and ending with पिशाच; here are अणिमा and seven other ऐश्वर्यस्; there are three गुणस् pervading here--Satva, etc.; realised not by eyes, but by experience. वा. १०२. ९६-8.
(II)--पैशाच, राक्षस, गान्धर्व, Kau- bera, Aindra, Saumya, प्राजापत्य, and ब्राह्म; a yogi must give up all these स्थानस् to attain the Brahmanhood. वा. १२. ३९-42; ६१. १७०; १०२. ९६-8.
--a Pravara of Angiras. M. १९६. १५. [page२-129+ ३७]
--bathing a deity; described. M. २६७. 1-३५.

--the entrance on the north side of the city of पुरञ्जन,
1: भा. IV. २५. ५१; २९. १२.
allegorically the left ear.

(I)--a daughter of स्वायम्भुव Manu, and sister of Priyavrata and उत्तानपाद; wife of Kardama and mother of Kapila;
1: भा. II. 7. 3; III. १२. २७, ५५-6; २१. 3; २२. 9; VIII. 1. 5.
heard of Kardama's greatness from नारद and fixed her mind on him; accepted by Kardama; seeing her playing with balls in her mansion विश्वावसु fell down in a fit of stupour; married Kardama with gifts from her parents; devoted herself to her husband's service like पार्वती to शिव; enjoyed his company in an aerial car well furnished with new cloths and ornaments after her bath in the सरस्वतिसरस्, where she was attended by many maids; roamed in all lovely parks throughout the earth. After a hundred years of enjoyment देवहूती gave birth to nine daughters at a time, when Kardama told her of his depar- ture for yoga; देवहूती requested means for protection of herself and the new-born ones; was told that विष्णु would be born in her womb and he would bring comfort to her. Soon she gave birth to Lord Kapila when ब्रह्मा and other seers called on Kardama. After they left, Kardama got his daughters married, and after praising Kapila, and with his permission he went away for penance. Heard all relating to the साङ्ख्य शास्त्र from Kapila and spoke in praise of him. Following the path prescribed by Kapila she attained निर्- वाण। The place where she attained siddhi became known as शिद्धपद।
2: Ib. VIII. Chh. २२ to २४ (whole); ३३. 1-३१; IV. I. 1 and १०.
From her, Hari manifested Himself for imparting धर्म and ज्ञान।
3: Ib. VIII. 1. 5.
(II)--the wife of पुरूरवस्. वा. 2. १६. [page२-130+ २२]
--the father of योगेश्वर. भा. VIII. १३. ३२.
--in the सालग्राम; here नागराट् takes the पिण्ड of the deserving and rejects that of the undeserving. Br. III. १३. ९०.
--playing grounds of the Devas--four; Caitraratha,^8 Nandana, वैभ्राज and Saviturvana (garden of the Sun). वा. ३६. १०.
--abodes of the Devas; meddling with, was punished by death. M. २२७. १७४.
(I)--a son of Krodhana and father of ऋष्य. भा. IX. २२. ११. Vi. IV. २०. 5.
(II)--a son of Akrodhana. M. ५०. ३७; वा. ९९. २३२.
(I)--a Mt. in कुशद्वीप. भा. V. २०. १५.
(II)--a son of क्षेमधन्व and father of अनीह (अहीनगु-ब्र्। प्।, अहीनक-वि। प्।). भा. IX. १२. 2; Br. III. ६३. २०३; M. १२. ५३; वा. ८८. २०३; Vi. IV. 4. १०६. [page२-131+ ३२]
(III)--a son of (Dharma) सावर्ण Manu. वा. १००. ८४. Vi. III. 2. ३२.
--a son of Auttama Manu. वा. ६२. ३४.
--a son of कालनेमि. Br. III. 5. ३९; वा. ६७. ८०.

(I)--a son of प्रतीप and brother of शन्तनु; renounced the home and turned मुनि; requested by शन्तनु to take up the throne; he spoke impeaching the Vedas. He took to yoga living in कलापग्राम. He was to establish the Lunar race in the कृत Yuga; Purohita of the Devas;
1: भा. IX. २२. १२-18; XII. 2. ३७; वा. ९९. २३४.
un- acceptable to the people as he suffered from leprosy.
2: M. ५०. ३९-41; २७३. ५६.
A राजऋषि and a gotrapravartaka of the Treta yuga
3: वा. ३२. ३९.
and a Paurava.

(II)--a Paurava king who continues to live in Kali in कलापग्राम; क्षत्रप्रणेतार in the २४थ् Catur- yuga. Originator of क्षत्रियस् in the कृत.
1: वा. ९९. ४३७-8; Vi. IV. २४-118.
A son of Pra- तीप. Even as a child retired to forest. The famine in his brother Santanu's (s.v) kingdom was said to be due to his elder brother देवापि having been passed over for succes- sion. Infected with heretical views through the minister of शन्तनु by means of ascetics in the forest; thus disquali- fied for the throne.
2: Vi. IV. २०. 9-३०.
--a Mt. with a Janapada on it; afraid of Hira- ण्यकशिपु's prowess. M. १६३. ८८. [page२-132+ २८]
--a son of Uttama Manu. Br. II. ३६. ३९.
--a great forest on the banks of the लौहित्या lake. वा. ४७. ११.
--one of the ten sons of हृदीक. Father of कम्बलबर्हिष. M. ४४. ८२-3; वा. ९६. १३९; Vi. IV. १४. २४.
--a Mt. of क्रौञ्चद्वीप. M. १२२. ८२.

(I)--a son of सात्वत and father of Babhru; equal to Gods;
1: भा. IX. २४. 6-१०; Vi. IV. १३. 1-3.
sonless he performed penance on the banks of the पर्णाशा (s.v.) which became transformed into a maid, married him and became mother of Babhru.
2: Br. III. ७१. १६-15; M. ४४. ४७-59; वा. ९६. 6-१५.
The वायु पुराण says that when he made austerities, he touched the waters of the सवऋणा when सावित्री appeared as a lady, received his तेजस् and brought forth a good son in the ninth month. This was Babhru.
2: Br. III. ७१. १६-15; M. ४४. ४७-59; वा. ९६. 6-१५.
Belonged to the Anu line and was much praised by poets and scholars. ६६०८ disciples of his, obtained immortality.
3: Vi. IV. १३. 6.
--building of temples, an act of cha- rity. Br. IV. 7. ३३.

(II)--a sacred तीर्थ, where there is a well by name वृष;
1: Br. III. १३. ४१; वा. ७७. ४१.
on her banks was वीरनगर.
2: Vi. II. १५. 6.
--a तीर्थम् sacred to नन्दिनी. M. १३. ३८.
--sacred to ललिता-pi1t2ham. Br. IV. ४४. ९६.
(I)--the first charioteer; a शक्ति. Br. IV. 6. १७; २०. ९१.
(III)--an Apsaras. वा. ६९. 6.
--the observance of this vow leads to the world of लक्ष्मी. M. १०१. ५९.
--utterance of, in दीक्षा। Br. IV. ४३. ११.
--Gods of prime importance, of secondary importance; share in sacrifices; they are Gurus, Lords, Kings and Forefathers; protect the subjects. वा. ६४. २१-23.
--वैभ्राज, Surabhi, Caitraratha, विशोक, Sumana and Nandana gardens. Br. III. 7. १०१-2.
--in सिद्धिक्षेत्र; here ईश्वर performed austerities standing on one leg. वा. ७७. ८१.
